utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. Please be seated. May we please hear the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is case number IT-96-23/2-I, the Prosecutor of the Tribunal against Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much, and may we have the appearances in this case. For the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Peggy Kuo on behalf of the Prosecution. With me is Diane Dicklich, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Defence counsel. Microphone for the Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. DUBOIS
utterances.text: Nobody tell me the microphone. Excuse me, Your Honour. I'm Valerie Dubois, lawyer in Paris, and I assist Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please, let's be sure that everybody can understand us. Mr. Stankovic, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then may I ask the Defence: Did you receive the necessary documents in preparation of this Initial Appearance?

utterances.speaker: MS. DUBOIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to discuss the material with the accused?

utterances.speaker: MS. DUBOIS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I please speak in French? Because my English would be inadequate. I saw Mr. Stankovic half an hour ago. He does not wish me to represent him during this hearing, but I explained to him that this was regular procedure and that he will have time to prepare his defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. We received the document in which it is stated that Mr. Stankovic said that he didn't want an attorney to represent him at the Initial Appearance in court. He will select an attorney of his own choosing later. Nevertheless, under Article 11 of the directive on assignment of Defence counsel, in the interests of justice, the Registrar has assigned you for this Initial Appearance today. Let me now turn to Mr. Stankovic, who is appearing on the basis of the amended indictment of the 5th of October, 1999. As far as I know - and OTP, please correct me if I'm wrong - he was arrested the 9th of July. The legal basis was an arrest warrant dated the 5th of July, 2002. Mr. Stankovic was brought to The Hague and is, since Wednesday, in the United Nations Detention Unit in Scheveningen. This case was assigned by the President of this Tribunal to Trial Chamber II. In this context, I have already now to inform the parties that Trial Chamber II is composed of Judge Agius, Judge Mumba, and me. We have checked whether or not there could be an obstacle to act as Judges in this case. As to the fact that Judge Mumba had been Presiding Judge in the case against Mr. Kunarac and others, and me myself been on the Bench in the appeals case against Mr. Kunarac and others. Nevertheless, we came to the conclusion that, especially under Rule 15, this does not create an obstacle, at any rate, not for the purposes of an Initial Appearance. Nevertheless, it might be that the assignment to Trial Chamber II is a provisional only. Mr. Stankovic, I should like to ask you several questions. The first questions are only for purposes of the identification, having nothing to do with the case as such. Would you please state your full name, including all first names and last names, for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Radovan Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And your father's and mother's name, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Todor and Petra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And what is the date and place of your birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 10th of March, 1969, in the village of Trebica, the Foca municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And what was your professional occupation before you came here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last occupation was policeman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Your last place of residence, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Srbinje, Foca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And finally, are you married and do you have children?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am. I have two sons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stankovic. The proceedings today are your Initial Appearance before this Tribunal. It seems, first of all, to be a formality only, but it is very important in time, setting to a certain extent the course for the entire procedure. The underlying reasons for this procedure is the following: The Prosecution has asked the Trial Chamber to confirm an indictment against you, on a prima facie basis. Additionally, there was a request for an arrest warrant forming the basis of your deprivation of your liberty. Normally, the other party, in this case you, Mr. Stankovic, would have a right to be heard before a decision is taken. But it is in the nature of the aforementioned decisions that it was not possible to hear you beforehand. This will be cured now. You will have the possibility to contest both the indictment and the deprivation of liberty. For a better understanding of what's going on, let me give you the following information before the reading out of the indictment: Mr. Stankovic, it is your right to remain silent. No inference to your disadvantage can be drawn if you remain totally silent. The inference can be drawn, the only one, can be found in Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, where you can read that: "if the accused fails to enter a plea in the Initial Appearance, the judge shall enter a plea of not guilty on the accused's behalf." But I have to warn you at the same time that everything you may say in the courtroom may be used even against you in evidence. Mr. Stankovic, did you understand this admonition?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's now hear the charges of the indictment, but only in those parts relevant for Mr. Stankovic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to her authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the Tribunal charges Radovan Stankovic with crimes against humanity and violations of the laws or customs of war, as set forth below: Background. The city and municipality of Foca are located south-east of Sarajevo, in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and borders Serbia and Montenegro. According to the 1991 census, the population of Foca consisting of 40.513 persons was 51.6 per cent Muslim, 45.3 per cent Serbian, and 3.1 per cent others. The political and military takeover of the municipality of Foca started with the first military actions in the town of Foca on 7 April 1992. The Serb forces, supported by artillery and heavy weapons, proceeded to take over Foca, section by section. The takeover of Foca town was complete by 16 or 17 April 1992. The surrounding villages continued to be under siege until mid-July 1992. As soon as the Serb forces had taken over parts of Foca town, military police, accompanied by local and non-local soldiers started arresting Muslim and Croat inhabitants. Until mid-July 1992, they continued to round up and arrest Muslim villagers from the surrounding villages in the municipality. The Serb forces separated men and women and unlawfully confined thousands of Muslims and Croats in various short and long-term detention facilities or kept them essentially under house arrest. During the arrests, many civilians were killed, beaten, or subjected to sexual assault. The Foca Kazneno-Popravni Dom hereinafter KP Dom, one of the largest prison facilities in the former Republic of Yugoslavia was the primary detention facility for men. Muslim women, children, and the elderly were detained in houses, apartments, and motels in the town of Foca or in surrounding villages, or at short and long-term detention centres such as Buk Bijela, Foca High School, and Partizan Sports Hall, respectively. Many of the detained woman were subjected to humiliating and degrading conditions of life, to brutal beatings and to sexual assaults, including rapes. Besides the above-mentioned detention places, several woman were detained in houses and apartments used as brothels, operated by groups of soldiers, mostly paramilitary. The ICRC and other organisation, unaware of these detention facilities, did not intervene. Therefore, those detainees had no possibility of release or exchange. The accused. Radovan Stankovic, aka Rasa, son of Todor, born on 12 February 1969 in the village of Trebica, municipality of Foca, was a permanent resident of Miljevina. He belonged to the Serb elite paramilitary unit of Pero Elez. Radovan Stankovic was also a subordinate of Pero Elez. Radovan Stankovic was in charge of Karaman's house in Miljevina, where Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Muslim women were detained and sexually assaulted, including raped. General allegations. At all times relevant to this indictment, an armed conflict existed in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the territory of the former Yugoslavia. At all times relevant to this indictment, the accused were required to abide by the laws or customs governing the conduct of war. Unless otherwise set forth below, all acts and omissions set forth in this indictment took place between April 1992 and February 1993. In each count charging crimes against humanity, a crime recognised by Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal, the acts or omissions were part of a widespread or large-scale or systematic attack against a civilian population, specifically the Muslim population of the municipality of Foca. Witnesses and victims are identified in this indictment using code-names or pseudonyms, such as FWS-95 or initials, for example, DB. All accused are individually responsible for the crimes charged against them in this indictment, pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Individual criminal responsibility includes committing, planning, initiating, ordering or aiding and abetting in the planning, preparation, or execution of any acts or omissions set forth below. The charges. Counts 45 to 48. Enslavement and rape of FWS-75, FWS-87, and seven other women in Karaman's house. Pero Elez, a Serb paramilitary leader in a position of regional authority, commanded an elite unit of Vukovar fighters. Pero Elez's headquarters were in the Miljevina hotel. On 2nd of August, 1992, Dragoljub Kunarac, in concert with Pero Elez, took FWS-75, FWS-87, and DB from the Montenegrin headquarters in Foca to the Miljevina hotel because the women had spoken to journalists the day before about the living conditions in Partizan Sports Hall. Pero Elez ordered the detention of the three women in a house, which was close to the hotel, and owned by Nusret Karaman, a Muslim who lived in Germany. Later on, other women and girls were detained at Karaman's house. Some were as young as 12 and 14 years of age. The number of women and girls detained at Karaman's house between 2nd of August, 1992 and at least until 30 October, 1992 totalled nine. Radovan Stankovic, a soldier from the elite unit commanded by Pero Elez, was in charge of Karaman's house after the death of Pero Elez. Radovan Stankovic ran Karaman's house similar to a brothel. In contrast to Partizan Sports Hall, the detainees at Karaman's house had sufficient food. They were not guarded or locked inside the house. The detainees even had a key they could use to lock the door and prevent soldiers, not belonging to Pero Elez's group, from entering. The detainees were also given the telephone number of the Miljevina motel and were told that they should call this number if any soldier without authorisation tried to enter the house. When the women did call this number, either Radovan Stankovic or Pero Elez would come to prevent other persons from entering the house. Although the detainees were not guarded, they could not escape. They had nowhere to go, as they were surrounded by Serbs, both soldiers and civilians. FWS-75 and FWS-87 were detained in Karaman's house between or about 3 August until or about 30 October 1992, together with seven other women. Pero Elez treated the women as his personal property. During the entire period of their detention at Karaman's house, FWS-75, FWS-87, and the other female detainees were subjected to repeated rapes and sexual assaults at night. All the perpetrators were Serb soldiers who belonged to Pero Elez's group. Among the soldiers who frequently raped FWS-75 and FWS-87 (vaginal and anal penetration) was Radovan Stankovic. The first time both women were raped in Karaman's house was on or about 3 August 1992, shortly after their arrival. An unidentified soldier raped FWS-75 (vaginal penetration) while Radovan Stankovic raped FWS-87 that day. In addition to the rapes and other sexual assaults, all the female detainees were forced to work for the Serb soldiers, washing uniforms, cooking, and cleaning the house. FWS-87 was taken three times from Karaman's house to other buildings in Miljevina. On these occasions, she was forced to clean rooms in the buildings, cook for the soldiers, and paint the window frames. On one of the three occasions, when she was taken out with another woman, two Montenegrin soldiers sexually assaulted both women. At Karaman's house, the detainees constantly feared for their lives. If any woman refused to obey orders, she would be beaten. Soldiers often told the women that they would be killed after the soldiers were finished with them because they knew too much. FWS-87 felt suicidal during the entire time of her detention in Karaman's house. By the foregoing acts and omissions, Radovan Stankovic committed: Count 45 (enslavement). Count 45: Enslavement, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(C) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 46 (rape). Count 46: Rape, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 47 (rape). Count 47: Rape, a violations of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 48 (outrages upon personal dignity). Count 48: Outrages upon personal dignity, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute. Signed Carla Del Ponte, Prosecutor, dated this 5th day of October, 1999, at The Hague, the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stankovic, may I ask you: Did you understand this indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have to inform you that under Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, within 30 days of this Initial Appearance you will be called upon to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count but that should you so request, you may immediately enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on one or more counts. Mr. Stankovic, are you ready to enter a plea to the charges today? Are you able to tell us --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Do I have to stand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not wish -- I do not wish to plead to any of these charges and counts. I am guilty because I am Serb and because I defended my people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Wait a minute. You may come later with these remarks. First of all, I have formally to ask you, and I repeat: Are you ready to enter a plea to the charges today or do you want to wait the 30 days?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not wish to plea at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Did you discuss this with your Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Ms. Dubois, do you want to comment?

utterances.speaker: MS. DUBOIS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stankovic didn't -- I have nothing to add to what I said before with respect to my meeting with Mr. Stankovic that I had earlier on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this. Mr. Stankovic, the Rules state quite clearly that only if you request, then you may immediately enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on one or more count. Did I understand you correctly that you request to answer or not answer today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already answered that question. I do not wish to enter a plea at all with respect to this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I understand correctly that neither today, nor within the next 30 days, you want to enter a plea. Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then I have to inform you that under Rule 62, it reads: "if the accused fails to enter a plea at the initial or any further appearance, the judge has to enter a plea of not guilty on the accused's behalf." Do you understand the consequences, that your silence will be regarded as a plea of not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have the impression that the accused has understood the admonition and voluntarily decided not to enter a plea, neither today nor within the next 30 days, and therefore Rule 62 is applicable. And on behalf of the accused, it is to enter a plea of not guilty. This is true for all the counts in the indictment just read out. Therefore, the accused pleads not guilty to count 45, enslavement, a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(c) of the Statute of the Tribunal; to count 46 (rape), a crime against humanity, punishable under Article 5(g) of the Statute of the Tribunal; count 47, rape, a violation of the laws or customs of law, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal; and finally, to count 48, outrages upon personal dignity, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 of the Statute of the Tribunal. We may now turn to the question of deprivation of liberty. Today I have to decide whether or not there will be an ongoing deprivation of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. your liberty. Of course, it's your right to contest the legality of your arrest. Do you want to raise any objections today or, as it is custom in this Tribunal, file a motion with the assistance of a Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will do so with the assistance of Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Therefore, then, I have today to order that the detention has to continue until further order and expect your contributions. Is it necessary that anybody is informed on your deprivation of liberty, for example, spouse or relative, especially to inform where you can be reached here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My family has already been informed, so that there's no need for you to inform them again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. In this context, the second question is: Do you want the Tribunal to inform your consulate or embassy on your deprivation of liberty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So please tell me what's the consulate or the embassy to be informed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I understand the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina entity Republika Srpska. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina will be informed. Do you want to add anything else? I have to ask you: What about your health condition and the condition in the Detention Unit? Do you have any observations as regards this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is fine. I have no observation whatsoever. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I then turn to the Office of the Prosecutor. I think on the basis of the remaining indictment before us, the OTP should be invited to rethink the question of jurisdiction in this case. No doubt the alleged crimes are serious crimes. They are serious war crimes, if they are committed as described in the indictment. Nevertheless, the test whether or not we have jurisdiction, of course, remains the one we already can read in the entire, full name of our Tribunal: Serious violations of international humanitarian law. And in addition, we have to check, especially taking into account the situation in the Detention Unit and the long period of detention, trial pending, being aware of all the other cases waiting to be heard, whether or not there is a concurrent jurisdiction able and willing to hear this case, and in this respect to revisit whether or not Rule 11 bis of our Rules of Procedure could be applicable in this case. Any comments from the OTP at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of the Prosecution, I wish to state that we do regard these allegations as being serious violations, and they are part of an indictment that was previously found -- where the accused were previously found to be guilty, and that was affirmed on appeal. However, we do -- we will take Your Honour's comments into consideration, and I will bring this to the attention of those who are able to make a decision whether this rethinking is necessary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any other observations by the parties? This seems not to be the case. I have to thank you for being here, and this concludes the Initial Appearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: adjourned at 9.36 a.m.
